pages.text: "The market!" Lulu hopped before the main road. Today Mom and the cousins had come downhill to shop. Lulu wanted to hurry across to the market.
Mom took the cousins' hands one by one. But eager Lulu stepped onto the main road alone. Mom quickly caught Lulu's hand. "Wait, Lulu!"
Just then, an old car roared past right in front. Lulu pressed against Mom's leg, long ears flat back. "...I did not see it, Mom."
Mom crouched before Lulu. "Your ears are very long. Even before seeing a car, you can hear it." Lulu touched an ear. "My ears?"
"Stop before the road and prick them up." Lulu raised both ears. A distant engine rumbled. "Mom, a car is coming!"
The car passed. The road was quiet again. Lulu heard no sound now. "Ears up, then cross!" Lulu held Mom's hand.
Holding her hand tightly, Lulu crossed with steady steps. Ears up, eyes left and right. The cousins crossed together behind.
On the other side, Lulu's bell jingled. "I did not run alone!" Lulu raised both shoulders. Mom patted the back.
Now Lulu never ran before the main road. "One, stop before the road! Two, ears up, look left and right! Three, hold Mom's hand and walk steadily!" Returning, Lulu stopped first.
Mom hugged Lulu to her chest. "You stopped so well." Even in a hurry, stop before the road, raise your ears, and look both ways. "Ears up, then cross!" Lulu's ears stood above the apron.
